body:
@kitbdev  I understand your reasons. Nevertheless, there are also good reasons for changing `clear()`:


#### `editable` dependency
Whether undo history is cleared should not rely on a flag that is not directly related to it may not be a good implementation.
Tying undo history clearing to `editable` is an arbitrary implementation detail rather than an intuitive design pattern.
This is likely to cause confusion when the `editable` status changes at runtime and `clear()` suddenly clears the history — or fails to do so.


#### Backward compatibility
The actual biggest issue with this change is backward compatibility.
If backward compatibility is the absolute priority, the resolution leans toward updating the official documentation to accurately reflect the conditional behavior rather than changing code that existing projects might rely on.


#### Future
However, I apprehend that adjusting the documentation text would provoke that any change about `clear()`‘s behaviour would get even harder and much more unlikely to be feasible, since developer would rely on the actual behaviour _and_ the documentation text. So, probably this should be decided _before_ changing either documentation or behaviour.


#### Past
`clear()` did clear undo history before https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/56720, a PR that intendet to make context menu "Clear" more user friendly. Changing `clear()` to the current behaviour was probably a side effect.


___


> The clear menu option and the clear method should do the same thing.

Though this is an argument that should be said, I guess this wouldn‘t be an actual problem, since it would solve more problems. Also, this should not cause any architectural problem.


> Clearing the text without clearing the undo history is useful, this makes it unexposed (though there are other ways to do it).

Well, may be I understood something wrong, but couldn‘t I do `text = ""`? And, if needed `merge_overlapping_carets()`?


> The documentation is wrong regardless since it does not "Performs a full reset of TextEdit", which to me implies it would reset all values to default when it actually just clears the text and things like gutter line data and background color.

Background color? Does it actually clear background color? I don‘t think so.
Anyway, for me, "Performs a full reset of TextEdit" means resetting state without changing set values, but that’s a thing of interpretation. It‘s always good to specify the documentation so no interpretation is needed.

> Backward compatibility

Compatibility is a primary concern here.
I don't think we should change it just to fix the inconsistency.

> Background color? Does it actually clear background color? I don‘t think so.

I was thinking it clears line backgrounds since its saved per line in TextEdit::Text, but I guess it doesn't. It probably should.

> However, I apprehend that adjusting the documentation text would provoke that any change about clear()‘s behaviour would get even harder and much more unlikely to be feasible, since developer would rely on the actual behaviour and the documentation text. So, probably this should be decided before changing either documentation or behaviour.

In the future when we can break compatibility this can be revisited, but its not really a concern for now.

> Changing clear() to the current behaviour was probably a side effect.

The PR was approved, and it was a while ago. We can't really say changing the exposed method was just a side effect.

> Well, may be I understood something wrong, but couldn't I do `text = ""`? And, if needed `merge_overlapping_carets()`?

Calling `text = ""` is not enough, you also need to clear any data from each gutter.
